messages:
incident-bot: Paging: SEV2 alert triggered for service=embeddings-reranker, symptom=500/502 spike on /batch endpoint. Auto-assign -> eng-oncall. Incident channel: #incidents.

Sara: I’m on it (sara). Seeing 502s from the batch endpoint, started ~2026-07-15 12:02 UTC. Affects ~18% of batch requests. Putting a note on customer-ops.

Linh: Linh here — can you paste logs? I’ll check the reranker consumer.

Sara: Pasting top error lines (redacted):
```
2026-07-15T12:02:06Z ERROR batch_processor - request_id=abc123 - handler=process_batch - error=VectorSizeMismatch
  expected_dim=768 actual_dim=1024 batch_index=7
2026-07-15T12:02:06Z ERROR grpc - upstream_status=500 - downstream=reranker-v2 - trace=xxxyyy
```

Mike: I’m looking at the client side that assembles batches — we deployed a routing tweak at 11:58 that changed model variant mapping (v2 vs v2-quant). Hypothesis: mixed model variants ended up in the same batch.

Linh: Good call. Reranker expects uniform vector dims per batch. If a request mixed unquantized (1024) and quantized (768) outputs, the merger will blow up.

Sara: Timeline (quick):
- 11:56 UTC: canary rollout of routing rule to send heavy-queries to reranker-v2-quant
- 11:58 UTC: rule promoted to 25%
- 12:01 UTC: first 502 spike observed by frontend metric
- 12:02 UTC: SEV2 alert fired
- 12:09 UTC: rolled routing rule back to 0%
- 12:14 UTC: partial mitigation by disabling batching for the affected pool

Mike: Attaching a sample problematic batch payload (sanitized):
```
{
  "batch_id": "b-2026-07-15-0001",
  "entries": [
    {"id":"a1","vector_dim":768},
    {"id":"a2","vector_dim":1024},
    {"id":"a3","vector_dim":768}
  ]
}
```

Linh: That payload matches the error. If the batch processor doesn't validate dims before concat, it will attempt to create a single tensor and fail.

Sara: Immediate mitigation we did:
- Rolled routing rule back (11:09).
- Disabled batch aggregation for this customer pool and switched them to per-item calls (12:14).
- Added a short-term rate cap to reduce retries (12:16).

Customer-ops: Impact summary for customers so far?

customer-ops: A handful of customers on dedicated batches saw elevated 5xxs and retry storms. One SLA-sensitive tenant reported degraded throughput (support ticket #C-4421). No data exfiltration or PII exposure.

Mike: Next steps (in-incident RCA coordination):
1) Collect router + batch-assembler logs for the 11:50-12:20 window (Sara, Linh)
2) Export batch payloads (sanitized) for failing requests (Sara)
3) Add instrumentation to detect mixed-dim batches at ingestion (short-term guard)
4) Code fix: batch_processor should validate dims and either split mixed batches or fail gracefully with clear error (post-mortem task)
5) Re-run canary in staging with synthetic mixed-dim scenarios before any re-deploy of routing rule

Linh: I’ll start a grep for `VectorSizeMismatch` across the reranker fleet and dump traces tied to those trace IDs.

Sara: Ingress logs for router: `rt-01` shows 120 matching requests during window, 22 failed. Uploading the S3 link: https://s3.redwood/internal/incidents/1767324456/router-logs-clip.txt (redacted).

Mike: I’ll prepare a short patch to add pre-aggregation validation in the batch assembler. ETA ~40m. If deploy looks risky, we can hotpatch to return 400 on mixed batches to avoid 5xx ripples.

Linh: Hypotheses we want to track (putting them here so we can mark status):
- H1: routing rule sent mixed model variants into same batch -> confirmed by sample payload (status: Likely)
- H2: batch_processor lacked validation for vector dims -> confirmed (status: Confirmed)
- H3: a downstream model change changed vector size without updating catalog metadata -> investigating (status: Investigating)

Sara: I checked model registry: reranker-v2-quant schema lists dim=768, reranker-v2 lists dim=1024. Catalog showed both as active under the rule during 11:58-12:09. So H3 is possible but origin is the routing rule change.

incident-bot: Notify: on-call handoff scheduled in 1h. Use `/handoff` to pass to next oncall.

Oncall-lead: Jordan will take primary after 12:50 UTC. Please prepare a concise handoff note.

Mike: Patch ready for review — PR #7423. Adds: early-detection in batch_assembler, test coverage, metric `mixed_batch_count`. Requesting expedited review.

Sara: Deploying hotfix to staging canary now. If green, we’ll push to prod for the batch-assembler only (no routing changes).

Linh: I found two commits in the model deployment pipeline earlier this week that touched embedding dim metadata for reranker-v2-quant; owner is @jordan-models. Pulling the deploy logs.

Jordan: confirming I pushed a metadata tweak last Wednesday (non-breaking) to normalize naming. I didn’t change dims. I’ll standby to help with the metadata audit.

Mike: Mitigation status update (12:40 UTC):
- Routing rule rolled back -> traffic back to baseline
- Batch aggregation disabled for affected pools -> 5xxs dropped from 18% -> 2%
- Hotfix in staging (pre-aggregation validation) -> tests pass

Sara: Putting an in-incident checklist for the handoff to Jordan:
- Links: router logs clip, batch payload samples, PR #7423, failing trace IDs (list attached)
- Current mitigation: batching disabled + routing rollback
- Outstanding: confirm whether any customer clients sent mixed-dim vectors (client-side bug) vs routing mixing model variants
- Post-incident tasks: make mixed-dim guard permanent, add pre-deploy model-dimension check in routing, run regression tests

Jordan: I’ll take this. Will own the follow-ups and coordinate with models team for metadata audit. Handoff notes acknowledged.

Sara: Thanks — leaving channel (sara) — summarizing final numbers in the postmortem later.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> Monitoring. Pager schedule updated.

Jordan: Added action items to ticket INC-1767324456, assigned to mike (hotfix), linh (logs/traces), jordan (models audit), sara (pm/coordinator). Will schedule RCA doc in #postmortems tomorrow.

Mike: Quick note for the RCA: include a short replay of the routing rule change, the guardrails that failed, and the customer impact table (timestamps + affected tenants).

customer-ops: Notifying a subset of affected customers with summary and ETA for fix.

Sara: Closing the active thread — follow-ups tracked in INC-1767324456.
